newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra pays A$55.8 mln to fund gun buy-back.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra pays A$55.8 mln to fund gun buy-back.

text.p: Australian Attorney-General Daryl Williams said on Tuesday the government would give state governments A$55.84 million for administration of the national guns buy-back programme.
"Arrangements are now being made to transfer a total of A$55.835 million to the jurisdictions," Williams said in a statement.

The money, raised through a one-off increase in the Medicare levy, would pay for new registration and licensing systems, administration of the scheme, and contributions to a national public education campaign on guns.
Williams said more than 192,000 firearms had been surrendered so far, resulting in total compensation to gun owners of about $84 million nationally.
The April massacre of 35 people by lone gunman Martin Bryant in the island state of Tasmania prompted the Australian government to form the national plan to ban rapid-fire guns.
The total cost to the government of the scheme, including compensation payments and education and national safety programme contributions, is expected to be about A$500 million.
